1.1: Sha’ul, an emissary of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ, by the desire of Elohim, and Timotiyos the brother, to the assembly of Elohim that is at Qorinth, with all the qodeshim who are in all Aḵaia:
1.2: Favor to you and peace from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Father and the Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ.
1.3: Baruḵ be the Elohim and Father of our Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ, the Father of compassion and Elohim of all comfort,
1.4: who is comforting us in all our pressure, enabling us to comfort those who are in every pressure, through the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by Elohim.
1.5: Because, as the sufferings of Mashiaḥ overflow in us, so our comfort also overflows through Mashiaḥ.
1.6: And if we suffer pressure, it is for your comfort and deliverance, being worked out in enduring the same sufferings which we also suffer. If we are comforted, it is for your comfort and deliverance.
1.7: And our expectation for you is steadfast, because we know that as you are sharing in the sufferings - so also in the comfort.
1.8: For we do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, of our pressure which came to us in Asia, that we were weighed down, exceedingly, beyond ability, so that we despaired even of life.
1.9: Indeed, we had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves but in Elohim who raises the dead,
1.10: who rescued us from so great a death, and does rescue, in whom we trust that He shall still rescue us,
1.11: you also helping together in prayer for us, that thanks shall be given by many on our behalf for the favor bestowed upon us through many.
1.12: For our boasting is this: the witness of our conscience that we behaved ourselves in the world in simplicity and sincerity of Elohim, not in fleshly wisdom but in the favor of Elohim, and much more toward you.
1.13: For we are writing none other to you than what you read or understand. Now I trust you shall understand, even to the end,
1.14: as also you have understood us in part, that we are your boast as you also are ours, in the day of the Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
1.15: And relying on this I intended to come to you before, that you might twice receive a favor,
1.16: and to pass your way into Makedonia, and again from Makedonia come to you, and to be sent by you on my way to Yahuḏah.
1.17: Since I intended this, did I do it lightly? Or what I plan, do I plan according to the flesh, that with me there should be Yes, Yes, and No, No?
1.18: But Elohim is trustworthy, that our word to you was not Yes and No.
1.19: For the Bĕn of Elohim, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ, who was proclaimed among you by us - by me, Sila, and Timotiyos - was not Yes and No, but in Him was Yes.
1.20: For as many promises are of Elohim, in Him they are Yes, and in Him Amĕn, to the esteem of Elohim through us.
1.21: But He who establishes us with you in Mashiaḥ and has anointed us is Elohim,
1.22: who also sealed us, and gave the Ruaḥ in our hearts as a pledge.
1.23: And I call Elohim as witness against my being, that to spare you I came no more to Qorinth.
1.24: Not that we rule over your belief, but we are fellow workers for your joy, for you stand by belief.

10.1: And I, Sha’ul, myself appeal to you, through the meekness and gentleness of Mashiaḥ - I who am indeed lowly when face to face with you, but bold toward you when absent!
10.2: But I pray, that when I am present, I might not be bold with that confidence by which I think to be bold against some who reckon us as if we walked according to the flesh.
10.3: For though we walk in the flesh, we do not fight according to the flesh.
10.4: For the weapons we fight with are not fleshly but mighty in Elohim for overthrowing strongholds,
10.5: overthrowing reasonings and every high matter that exalts itself against the knowledge of Elohim, taking captive every thought to make it obedient to ha’Mashiaḥ,
10.6: and being ready to punish all disobedience, when your obedience is complete.
10.7: Take a look at what you are facing. If anyone trusts in himself that he is of Mashiaḥ, let him reckon again for himself, that as he is of Mashiaḥ, so also are we.
10.8: For even if I should boast somewhat more about our authority, which the Aḏon gave us for building up, and not for overthrowing you, I shall not be put to shame,
10.9: lest I seem to frighten you away by letters.
10.10: Because they say, “His letters are truly weighty and strong, but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech amounts to naught.”
10.11: Let such a one take this into account, that what we are in word by letters when absent, such also in deed when we are present.
10.12: For we do not presume to count ourselves or compare ourselves with some of those who commend themselves. But they, measuring themselves by themselves, and comparing themselves among themselves, are not wise.
10.13: But we shall not boast beyond measure, but within the measure of the limits Elohim assigned unto us, to reach even to you.
10.14: For we are not overextending ourselves, as if we did not reach to you, for we also came to you with the Good News of ha’Mashiaḥ,
10.15: not boasting beyond measure in the labors of others, but having an expectation, that as your belief grows, we shall be greatly enlarged by you, according to our limits,
10.16: to bring the Good News in the parts beyond you - not to boast in another’s limits in what has been accomplished.
10.17: But “He who boasts, let him boast in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”
10.18: For not he who commends himself is approved, but he whom the Aḏon commends.

11.1: I would that you could bear with me in a little folly. But indeed, you are bearing with me.
11.2: For I am jealous for you with a jealousy according to Elohim. For I gave you in marriage to one husband, to present you as an innocent maiden to Mashiaḥ.
11.3: But I am afraid, lest, as the serpent deceived Ḥawwah by his trickery, so your minds should be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Mashiaḥ.
11.4: For, indeed, if he who is coming proclaims another 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, whom we have not proclaimed, or if you receive a different spirit which you have not received, or a different Good News which you have not accepted, you put up with it well enough!
11.5: For I reckon that I am not inferior to the most eminent emissaries.
11.6: But even if I am unskilled in word, yet not in knowledge. Indeed, in every way we have been manifested among you in all.
11.7: Or did I commit sin in humbling myself in order to exalt you, because I brought good news, the Good News of Elohim to you without being paid?
11.8: Other assemblies I robbed, by receiving wages to serve you.
11.9: And when I was present with you, and in need, I was not a burden to anyone, for what was lacking to me the brothers who came from Makedonia supplied. And in every way I kept myself - and shall keep - from being a burden to you.
11.10: It is a truth of Mashiaḥ in me, that this boasting in me shall not be stopped in the districts of Aḵaia.
11.11: Why? Is it that I do not love you? Elohim knows!
11.12: And I shall go on doing as I do, in order to cut off the occasion from those desiring an occasion, so that in that which they boast, they might be found also as we are.
11.13: For such are false emissaries, deceptive workers, masquerading as emissaries of Mashiaḥ.
11.14: And no wonder! For Satan himself masquerades as a messenger of light!
11.15: It is not surprising, then, if his servants also masquerade as servants of righteousness, whose end shall be according to their works!
11.16: Again I say, let no one think me to be a fool. And if otherwise, at least receive me as a fool, for me to also boast a little.
11.17: What I speak, I speak not according to the Aḏon, but as in foolishness, in this boldness of boasting.
11.18: Since many boast according to the flesh, I too shall boast.
11.19: For you, being wise, put up with fools gladly!
11.20: For you put up with it if anyone enslaves you, if anyone devours you, if anyone takes from you, if anyone exalts himself, if one hits you in the face.
11.21: To shame, I say that we were too weak for that! But in whatever anyone is bold - I say it in foolishness - I am bold also.
11.22: Are they Iḇrim? So am I. Are they Yisra’ĕlites? So am I. Are they the seed of Aḇraham? So am I.
11.23: Are they servants of Mashiaḥ? - I speak as beside myself - I am more, in labors much more, in stripes above measure, in prisons more frequently, in deaths many times.
11.24: Five times I received from the Yahuḏim forty stripes less one.
11.25: Three times I was beaten with rods, once I was stoned, three times I was shipwrecked, a night and a day I have been in the deep,
11.26: in many travels, in dangers of waters, in dangers of robbers, in dangers from my own race, in dangers from the gentiles, in dangers in the city, in dangers in the desert, in dangers in the sea, in dangers among false brothers;
11.27: in toil and hardship, in watchings often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness,
11.28: besides that from outside, what comes upon me daily: the anxiety for all the assemblies.
11.29: Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is made to stumble, and I do not burn?
11.30: If I have to boast, I shall boast of matters that show up my weakness.
11.31: The Elohim and Father of our Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ, who is baruḵ forever, knows that I am not lying.
11.32: In Dammeseq the governor, under Aretas the meleḵ, was guarding the city of the Damascenes, wanting to seize me,
11.33: but through a window I was let down in a basket by the wall, and escaped from his hands.

12.1: To boast, indeed, is useless for me, for I shall go on to visions and revelations of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
12.2: I know a man in Mashiaḥ who fourteen years ago - whether in the body I do not know, or whether out of the body I do not know, Elohim knows - such a one was caught up to the third shamayim.
12.3: And I know such a man - whether in the body or out of the body I do not know, Elohim knows -
12.4: that he was caught up into Paradise and heard unspeakable words, which it is not right for a man to speak.
12.5: Of such a one I shall boast, but of myself I shall not boast, except in my weaknesses.
12.6: For if I shall want to boast, I shall not be a fool, for I shall speak the truth. But I refrain, lest anyone should think more of me than what he sees in me, or hears of me.
12.7: And to keep me from exalting myself because of the exceeding greatness of the revelations, a thorn in the flesh was given to me, a messenger of Satan to hit me, to keep me from exalting myself.
12.8: Concerning this I pleaded with the Aḏon three times to take it away from me.
12.9: And He said to me, “My favor is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness.” Most gladly, then, I shall rather boast in my weaknesses, so that the power of Mashiaḥ rests on me.
12.10: Therefore I take pleasure in weaknesses, in insults, in needs, in persecutions, in distresses, for the sake of Mashiaḥ. For when I am weak, then I am strong.
12.11: I have become a fool - you have compelled me. For I should have been commended by you, for in no respect was I behind the most eminent emissaries, though I am a nobody.
12.12: Indeed, the signs of an emissary were wrought among you with all endurance, in signs and wonders and powers.
12.13: For what is there in which you were inferior to other assemblies, except that I myself was not a burden to you? Forgive me this wrong!
12.14: See, I am ready to come to you for the third time. And I shall not be a burden to you, for I do not seek yours, but you. For the children should not lay up for the parents, but the parents for the children.
12.15: And I shall most gladly spend and be spent for your lives. If I love you more and more, am I to be loved less?
12.16: But be it so, I did not burden you. But being crafty, did I catch you with guile?
12.17: Did I take advantage of you by any of those whom I sent to you?
12.18: I urged Titos, and sent our brother with him. Did Titos take advantage of you? Did we not walk in the same spirit - not in the same steps?
12.19: Again, do you think that we defend ourselves to you? We speak before Elohim in Mashiaḥ. But all this, beloved, is for your upbuilding.
12.20: For I fear lest, when I come, I do not find you such as I want, and I be found by you such as you do not want - lest there be strife, jealousies, outbursts of wrath, selfish ambitions, slander, gossip, puffings up, unrests,
12.21: and lest, when I come again, my Elohim should humble me among you, and I shall mourn for many who have sinned before and have not repented of the uncleanness, and whoring, and indecency which they have practiced.

13.1: This is the third time I am coming to you. “By the mouth of two or three witnesses every word shall be established.”
13.2: I have previously said, and I say beforehand, as being present the second time, and now being absent I write to those who have sinned before, and to all the rest, that if I come again I shall not spare,
13.3: since you are seeking for proof of Mashiaḥ speaking in me, who is not weak toward you, but mighty in you.
13.4: For though He was impaled in weakness, yet He lives by the power of Elohim. For we also are weak in Him, but we shall live with Him by the power of Elohim toward you.
13.5: Examine yourselves whether you are in the belief - prove yourselves. Or do you not know yourselves, that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ is in you, unless you are disapproved.
13.6: And I trust that you shall know that we are not disapproved.
13.7: And we pray to Elohim that you do no evil at all - not that we should appear approved, but that you should do what is right, even though we should appear unapproved.
13.8: For we have no power at all against the truth, but for the truth.
13.9: For we rejoice when we are weak and you are strong. And this also we pray for: your perfection.
13.10: For this reason I write this in my absence, so that, being present I should not use sharpness, according to the authority which the Aḏon has given me for upbuilding and not for overthrowing.
13.11: For the rest, brothers, rejoice. Be made perfect, be encouraged, be of one mind, live in peace. And the Elohim of love and peace shall be with you.
13.12: Greet one another with a qodesh kiss.
13.14: The favor of the Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ, and the love of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and the fellowship of the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh be with all of you. Amĕn.

2.1: And I decided this within myself, not to come to you again in sadness.
2.2: For if I make you sad, then who is he who makes me glad but the one who is made sad by me?
2.3: And I wrote to you as I did, so that having come, I might not have sadness over those from whom I should have joy, trusting in you all that my joy is that of you all.
2.4: For out of much pressure and distress of heart I wrote to you, with many tears, not that you should be sad, but that you might know the love which I so richly have for you.
2.5: But if anyone has caused sadness, he has not made me sad, but in some degree you all - not to be too harsh.
2.6: For such a one this punishment, by the many, is sufficient,
2.7: so that, on the contrary, you should rather forgive and comfort, lest somehow such a one be swallowed up with too much sadness.
2.8: So I appeal to you to confirm your love to him.
2.9: Besides, I wrote for this purpose also, that I might know the proof of you, if you are obedient in all.
2.10: And whom you forgive anything, I do also. For indeed, if I have forgiven anything, I have forgiven that one for your sakes in the sight of Mashiaḥ,
2.11: lest Satan should take advantage of us, for we are not ignorant of his thoughts.
2.12: And when I came to Troas for the Good News of Mashiaḥ, and a door was opened to me by the Aḏon,
2.13: I had no rest in my spirit, because I did not find Titos my brother. But taking my leave of them, I went on to Makedonia.
2.14: But thanks be to Elohim who always leads us on, to overcome in Mashiaḥ, and manifests through us the fragrance of His knowledge in every place.
2.15: Because we are to Elohim the fragrance of Mashiaḥ among those who are being saved and among those who are perishing.
2.16: To the one we are the smell of death to death, and to the other the fragrance of ḥai to ḥai. And who is competent for these?
2.17: For we are not, as so many, merchandising the Word of Elohim - but as of sincerity, but as from Elohim, in the sight of Elohim, we speak in Mashiaḥ.

3.1: Are we to begin to recommend ourselves again? Or do we need, as some, letters of recommendation to you, or from you?
3.2: You are our letter, having been written in our hearts, known and read by all men,
3.3: making it obvious that you are a letter of Mashiaḥ, served by us, written not with ink but by the Ruaḥ of the living Elohim, not on tablets of stone but on fleshly tablets of the heart.
3.4: And such trust we have toward Elohim, through ha’Mashiaḥ.
3.5: Not that we are competent in ourselves to reckon anything as from ourselves, but our competence is from Elohim,
3.6: who also made us competent as servants of a Renewed Covenant, not of the letter but of the Ruaḥ, for the letter kills but the Ruaḥ gives ḥai.
3.7: But if the administering of death in letters, engraved on stones, was esteemed, so that the children of Yisra’ĕl were unable to look steadily at the face of Mosheh because of the esteem of his face, which was passing away,
3.8: how much more esteemed shall the administering of the Ruaḥ not be?
3.9: For if the administering of condemnation had esteem, the administering of righteousness exceeds much more in esteem.
3.10: For indeed what was made esteemed had no esteem in this respect, in view of the esteem that excels.
3.11: For if that which is passing away was esteemed, much more that which remains in esteem.
3.12: Having then such expectation, we use much boldness of speech,
3.13: and not like Mosheh, who put a veil over his face so that the children of Yisra’ĕl should not look steadily at the end of what was passing away.
3.14: But their minds were hardened, for to this day, when the old Covenant is being read, that same veil remains, not lifted, because in Mashiaḥ it is taken away.
3.15: But to this day, when Mosheh is being read, a veil lies on their heart.
3.16: And when one turns to the Aḏon, the veil is taken away.
3.17: Now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is the Ruaḥ, and where the Ruaḥ of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is, there is freedom.
3.18: And we all, as with unveiled face we see as in a mirror the esteem of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, are being transformed into the same likeness from esteem to esteem, as from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the Ruaḥ.

4.1: Therefore, having this service, even as we received compassion, we do not lose heart,
4.2: but have renounced the secrets of shame, not walking in craftiness nor falsifying the Word of Elohim, but by the manifestation of the truth recommending ourselves to every human conscience, in the sight of Elohim.
4.3: And indeed, if our Good News has been veiled, it has been veiled in those who are perishing,
4.4: in whom the mighty one of this age has blinded the minds of the unbelieving, so that the enlightening of the Good News of the esteem of Mashiaḥ, who is the likeness of Elohim, does not shine on them.
4.5: For we do not proclaim ourselves, but Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 the Aḏon, and ourselves your servants for the sake of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
4.6: For Elohim, who said, “Let light shine out of darkness,” is the One who has shone in our hearts for the enlightening of the knowledge of the esteem of Elohim in the face of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ.
4.7: And we have this treasure in earthen vessels, so that the excellence of the power might be of Elohim, and not of us -
4.8: being hard pressed on every side, but not crushed; being perplexed, but not in despair;
4.9: being persecuted, but not forsaken; being thrown down, but not destroyed;
4.10: always bearing about in the body the dying of the Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, that the ḥai of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 might also be manifested in our body.
4.11: For we, the living, are always delivered to death for the sake of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, that the ḥai of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 might also be manifested in our mortal flesh,
4.12: so that death indeed is working in us, but the ḥai in you.
4.13: But having the same spirit of belief, according to what has been written, “I believed, therefore I spoke,” we also believe, therefore we also speak,
4.14: knowing that He who raised up the Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 shall also raise us up through 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, and shall present us with you.
4.15: For all this is for your sake, so that favor, having spread through the many, would cause thanksgiving to overflow, unto the esteem of Elohim.
4.16: Therefore we do not lose heart, but even if our outward man is perishing, yet that within is being renewed day by day.
4.17: For this slight momentary pressure, is working for us a far more exceeding and everlasting weight of esteem.
4.18: We are not looking on what is seen, but on what is not seen. For what is seen passes away, but what is not seen is everlasting.

5.1: For we know that if the tent of our earthly house, is destroyed, we have a building from Elohim, a house not made with hands, everlasting in the shamayim.
5.2: For indeed in this we groan, longing to put on our dwelling which is from shamayim,
5.3: if indeed, having put it on, we shall not be found naked.
5.4: For indeed, we who are in this tent groan, being burdened, not because we want to put it off, but to put on, so that what is to die might be swallowed up by ḥai.
5.5: Now He who has prepared us for this same purpose is Elohim, who has given us the Ruaḥ as a pledge of what is to come.
5.6: Therefore, being always of good courage, and knowing that while we are at home in the body we are absent from the Aḏon -
5.7: for we walk by belief, not by sight -
5.8: we are of good courage, and are well-pleased rather to be absent from the body and to be present with the Aḏon.
5.9: So we also make it our aim to be well-pleasing to Him, whether being at home, or being away from home.
5.10: For we all have to appear before the judgment seat of Mashiaḥ, in order for each one to receive according to what he has done in the body, whether good or evil.
5.11: Knowing, therefore, the reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, we persuade men, but we have been made manifest to Elohim, and I also trust in your consciences to have been manifested.
5.12: For we do not again commend ourselves to you, but give you an occasion to boast on our behalf, in order that you may have an answer for those who take pride in appearance and not in heart.
5.13: For whether we are beside ourselves, it was for Elohim, or whether we are of sound mind, it is for you.
5.14: For the love of Mashiaḥ compels us, having judged this: that if One died for all, then all died;
5.15: and He died for all, that those who live should no longer live for themselves, but for Him who died for them, and was raised.
5.16: So from now onwards we know no one according to the flesh. And if we have known Mashiaḥ according to the flesh, yet now we no longer know.
5.17: Therefore, if anyone is in Mashiaḥ, he is a renewed creature - the old have passed away, see, all have become renewed!
5.18: And all is from Elohim, who has restored us to favor with Himself through 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ, and has given us the service of restoration to favor,
5.19: that is, that Elohim was in Mashiaḥ restoring the world to favor unto Himself, not reckoning their trespasses to them, and has committed to us the word of restoration to favor.
5.20: Therefore we are envoys on behalf of Mashiaḥ, as though Elohim were pleading through us. We beg, on behalf of Mashiaḥ: Be restored to favor with Elohim.
5.21: For He made Him who knew no sin to be sin for us, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of Elohim.

6.1: And working together, we also call upon you not to receive the favor of Elohim in vain -
6.2: For He says, “In an acceptable time I have heard you, and in a day of deliverance I have helped you.” See, now is the well-accepted time, see, now is a day of deliverance -
6.3: giving no cause of stumbling in whatever, so that the service is not blamed.
6.4: Rather, we commend ourselves as servants of Elohim in every way: in much endurance, in pressures, in hardships, in distresses,
6.5: in stripes, in imprisonments, in disturbances, in toils, in watchings, in fastings,
6.6: in cleanness, in knowledge, in patience, in kindness, in the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh, in love unfeigned,
6.7: in the Word of truth, in the power of Elohim, through the weapons of righteousness, on the right and on the left,
6.8: through esteem and disrespect, through evil report and good report; as deceivers, and yet true;
6.9: as unknown, and yet well-known; as dying, and see, we live; as disciplined, and yet not killed;
6.10: as sad, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet enriching many; as having naught, and yet possessing all.
6.11: Our mouth has spoken openly to you, O Qorin’tiyim, our heart is wide open.
6.12: You are not restrained by us, but you are restrained by your own affections.
6.13: But for the same reward - I speak as to children - open wide yourselves too.
6.14: Do not become unevenly yoked with unbelievers. For what partnership have righteousness and lawlessness? And what fellowship has light with darkness?
6.15: And what agreement has Mashiaḥ with Beliya’al? Or what part does a believer have with an unbeliever?
6.16: And what union has the Mishkan of Elohim with idols? For you are a Mishkan of the living Elohim, as Elohim has said, “I shall dwell in them and walk among them, and I shall be their Elohim, and they shall be My people.”
6.17: Therefore, “Come out from among them and be separate, says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and do not touch what is unclean, and I shall receive you.
6.18: “And I shall be a Father to you, and you shall be sons and daughters to Me, says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Ĕl Shaddai.”

7.1: Having, then, these promises, beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all defilement of the flesh and spirit, perfecting qodeshah in the reverence of Elohim.
7.2: Make room for us, we wronged no one, we corrupted no one, we exploited no one.
7.3: I do not say this to condemn, for I previously said that you are in our hearts, to die together and to live together.
7.4: Great is my boldness of speech toward you, great is my boasting on your behalf. I have been filled with encouragement, I overflow with joy in all our pressure.
7.5: For, indeed, when we came into Makedonia, our flesh had no rest, but we were hard pressed on every side - conflicts without, fears within.
7.6: But Elohim, who encourages the downcast, encouraged us by the coming of Titos,
7.7: and not only by his coming, but also by the encouragement with which he was encouraged over you, when he reported to us your longing, your mourning, your ardor for me, so that I rejoiced even more.
7.8: For even if I made you sad with my letter, I do not regret it, though I did regret it. For I perceive that the same letter made you sad, even if for an hour.
7.9: I now rejoice, not that you were made sad, but that you were saddened into repenting. For you were made sad according to Elohim, so that you suffered no loss from us.
7.10: For sadness according to Elohim works repentance to deliverance, not to be regretted, but the sadness of the world works death.
7.11: For see how you have been saddened according to Elohim - how much eagerness it worked in you; indeed, clearing of yourselves; indeed, displeasure; indeed, reverence; indeed, longing; indeed, ardor; indeed, righting of wrong! In every way you proved yourselves to be clear in the matter.
7.12: So although I wrote to you, it was not for the sake of him who had done the wrong, nor for the sake of him who suffered wrong, but for the sake of revealing to you our diligence for you, before Elohim.
7.13: For this reason we have been encouraged in your encouragement. And we rejoiced exceedingly more for the joy of Titos, because his spirit has been refreshed by all of you.
7.14: Because if I have boasted somewhat about you to him, I am not ashamed. But as we spoke to you in all truth, even so our boasting to Titos was found true.
7.15: And his tender feelings are greater for you as he remembers the obedience of all of you, as you received him with fear and trembling.
7.16: I rejoice that in every way I am of good courage by reason of you.

8.1: Now brothers, we make known to you the favor of Elohim which has been given in the assemblies of Makedonia:
8.2: that in much trial of pressure the overflowing of their joy and their deep poverty overflowed into the riches of their generosity.
8.3: Because I bear witness that according to their ability, and beyond their ability, they gave voluntarily,
8.4: begging us with much urgency for the favor of taking part in this service to the qodeshim.
8.5: And, not as we had expected, they gave themselves first to the Aḏon, and then to us by the desire of Elohim,
8.6: that we should urge Titos, that as he had begun, so he would also complete this kind gift in you as well.
8.7: But as you excel in every way - in belief, and speech, and knowledge, and all diligence, and in your love for us - that you should excel in this kind gift as well.
8.8: I speak not by command, but I am proving the genuineness of your love by the eagerness of others.
8.9: For you know the favor of our Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ, that being rich, He became poor for your sake, so that you might become rich through His poverty.
8.10: And in this I give an opinion: It is to your advantage not only to be doing what you began and were desiring to do a year ago,
8.11: and now also complete the work, that as with readiness in desiring it, so there also should be a completion out of what you have.
8.12: For if the readiness is present, it is well received according to what one has, not according to what he does not have -
8.13: not, however, that others should be eased and you hard pressed,
8.14: but by fair sharing, that now at this time your plenty for their need, so that their plenty might also be for your need - that there might be fair sharing.
8.15: As it has been written, “He who gathered much did not have too much, and he who gathered little had not less.”
8.16: But thanks be to Elohim who puts the same eagerness for you into the heart of Titos.
8.17: Because he received the appeal, indeed, but being more eager, he went to you of his own accord.
8.18: And we sent with him the brother whose praise is in the Good News through all the assemblies,
8.19: and not only so, but who was also chosen by the assemblies to travel with us with this gift that is administered by us to the esteem of the Aḏon Himself, and your ready mind,
8.20: avoiding this: that anyone should blame us in this generous gift which is administered by us.
8.21: For we provide what is right, not only in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, but also in the sight of men.
8.22: And we sent with them our brother whom we have often proved eager in many ways, but now much more eager, because of the great reliance which we have in you.
8.23: As for Titos, he is my partner and fellow worker for you. As for our brothers, messengers of the assemblies, the esteem of Mashiaḥ.
8.24: Therefore show to them the proof of your love and of our boasting on your behalf, and in the presence of the assemblies.

9.1: Indeed, concerning the service to the qodeshim, it is unnecessary for me to write to you;
9.2: for I know your eagerness, about which I boast of you to the Makedonians, that Aḵaia was ready a year ago. And your ardor has stirred up most of them.
9.3: But I sent the brothers, lest our boasting on behalf of you should be made empty in this part, in order that, as I said, you may be ready,
9.4: lest if some Makedonians come with me and find you not ready, we - not to speak of you - should be put to shame in this confidence of boasting.
9.5: So I thought it necessary to appeal to the brothers to come to you in advance, and arrange your promised beraḵah beforehand - this to be ready as a beraḵah and not as greediness.
9.6: And this: He who sows sparingly shall also reap sparingly, and he who sows on beraḵah shall also reap on beraḵah.
9.7: Let each one give as he purposes in his heart, not of grief or of necessity, for Elohim loves a joyous giver.
9.8: And Elohim is able to make all favor overflow toward you, that you, always having all you need in every way, have plenty for every good work.
9.9: As it has been written, “He scattered abroad, He gave to the poor, His righteousness remains forever.”
9.10: And He who supplies seed to the sower, and bread for food, shall supply and increase the seed you have sown and increase the fruit of your righteousness,
9.11: being enriched in every way for all simplicity, which works out thanksgiving to Elohim through us.
9.12: Because the rendering of this service not only supplies the needs of the qodeshim, but also is overflowing through many thanksgivings to Elohim.
9.13: Through the proof of this service, they esteem Elohim on the submission of your confession to the Good News of Mashiaḥ, and generosity in sharing with them and all men,
9.14: and by their prayer for you, who long for you because of the exceeding favor of Elohim in you.
9.15: Thanks also to Elohim for His unspeakable gift!
